clue.text: Old crock struggling with Mephisto? Not me!

indicators.note: something struggling is thrashing about, so the remaining letters are thrown into a new order
'Not me' tells the solver to strike out those two letters from the setter's name

parts.note: the puzzle's own name, taken as written
taken as written, the letters to remove

explanation.surface: An elderly wreck of a man is battling the crossword, and the setter protests it isn't him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old crock' reads as a decrepit person; here it is literally an old pot.
explanation.definitionFit: A pithos is a large storage jar of ancient Greece, so an old piece of crockery.

clue.text: Complaint hits Posy badly

indicators.note: done badly, the letters of the phrase end up out of their proper order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles that a girl called Posy is being struck hard.
explanation.definitionFit: Phytosis is a disease caused by a parasitic plant or fungus, a medical complaint.

clue.text: Tipped number agreed with tabloid image

indicators.note: a column tipped over is turned upside down, so in a down clue the letters read the other way

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for number
OK means agreed
the i is a British tabloid-format newspaper

explanation.surface: A tipped-off number has been agreed with a red-top paper over a picture deal.
explanation.walkthrough: The i is a short-form British national daily printed in tabloid size.
explanation.definitionFit: Ikon is a variant spelling of icon, a religious image or picture.

clue.text: Fish: tons turning up around lake

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for tons

indicators.note: around means the word for turning up wraps itself about the abbreviation for lake

parts.note: to rout is to root or turn up ground, as a pig does with its snout
L is the abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: Tons of fish appear around a lake, read as a catch report.
explanation.walkthrough: Rout in Chambers also means to grub up earth, so 'turning up' is the routing.
explanation.definitionFit: A troutling is a young or small trout, a kind of fish.

clue.text: Body folds and ladies headed to another primarily

indicators.note: beheaded or headed here means the word loses its leading letter

parts.note: ladies are women; without the head letter W

indicators.note: primarily points to the first letters of the preceding words

parts.note: initial letters of the two words

explanation.surface: Ladies hand on folded body linen to another woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Omenta are folds of the peritoneum joining the stomach to other organs.

clue.text: With stuff on board for return, area block dead silly

definitions.text: With stuff on board for return

indicators.note: silly suggests the letters behave foolishly and land in a different order

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for area
taken as written

explanation.surface: A ship heading home with cargo aboard leaves a whole area blocked and dead.
explanation.definitionFit: A backloaded lorry or ship carries goods on its return journey rather than travelling home empty.

clue.text: Attacker up on legs

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the following words are read from the bottom of the column upwards

parts.note: re means on, concerning
pins is slang for legs

explanation.surface: An assailant leaps up on his legs to strike.
explanation.definitionFit: A sniper attacks from hiding by shooting at targets from a distance.

clue.text: Baldrick stokes remains of fire

parts.note: S is one symbol for the stokes, a unit of kinematic viscosity
ash is what is left after burning

explanation.surface: Baldrick, the dogsbody of TV's Blackadder, rakes the embers.
explanation.walkthrough: Baldrick looks like the Blackadder character; it is a variant spelling of baldric. The stokes is a physics unit.
explanation.definitionFit: A baldric is a belt or sash worn over the shoulder, used to carry a sword.

clue.text: Scottish shirt is on one in the RAF

parts.note: the 's of 'it's', short for is
erk is slang for an aircraftman in the Royal Air Force

explanation.surface: A Scots shirt is being worn by an airman.
explanation.definitionFit: Serk is the Scots word for a shirt or shift, a dialect garment.

clue.text: Opening of station eatery on former platform

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter
a caff is British slang for a cheap café
old means former

explanation.surface: A café opens at a station on an old railway platform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Platform' fits the station picture, but it is the stage for an execution here.
explanation.definitionFit: A scaffold is a raised platform, especially one used for executions or for builders.

clue.text: Fly after having left for day in harbour

indicators.note: this phrase asks for the letter for left to stand in place of the letter for day

parts.note: to herd in Chambers is to keep or tend, so to harbour
L is the abbreviation for left
D is the abbreviation for day

explanation.surface: An insect flies off into the harbour once the day is over.
explanation.definitionFit: Herl is the barb of a feather used in dressing anglers' flies, and an artificial fly made with it.

clue.text: Quality of dwelling within unopened semi men can supply

indicators.note: unopened means the first letter of the word is taken away
read as 'supplely', in a pliant manner, so the letters bend into a new order

parts.note: semi without its opening letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: The quality of a home within a semi-detached house that some men can provide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supply' looks like the verb; read it as the adverb from supple.
explanation.definitionFit: Immanence is the theological quality of being inherent, of indwelling or existing within something.

clue.text: Juveniles with yen for a little room in dwelling

indicators.text: with yen for a little room in
indicators.note: this phrase asks for one letter to replace another inside the word for a dwelling

parts.note: a roof over one's head is a home
Y is the abbreviation for yen
a little of room is its first letter

explanation.surface: Youngsters long for a small room in the family home.
explanation.definitionFit: Yoof is a jocular spelling of youth, meaning young people collectively.

clue.text: Row about boring Norfolk town almost leads to writ as before

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the town is dropped
something boring drills into another thing and sits inside it

parts.note: Diss is a market town in Norfolk; almost loses its final S
a string is a row or series
a is a Chambers abbreviation for about

explanation.surface: A quarrel about drilling in a Norfolk town almost ends in a lawsuit as before.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as before' marks the definition as historical: the writ is obsolete.
explanation.definitionFit: Distringas was a former writ directing a sheriff to distrain, that is, to seize goods.

clue.text: Indian clerk about to get annual return

parts.note: circ. is an abbreviation of circa, about
A is an abbreviation for annual
R is an abbreviation for return

explanation.surface: An Indian office worker is about to receive a yearly tax return.
explanation.walkthrough: 'annual return' looks like one company filing; it splits into two abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: Circar is a variant of sircar, an Anglo-Indian term for a house steward or accountant.

clue.text: Dull person, sort one rebuffed

indicators.note: rebuffed means pushed back, so the letters are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: a kind is a sort
'un is dialect for one, as in 'a good 'un'

explanation.surface: A boring person, a decent sort, is turned away.
explanation.definitionFit: Nudnik is Yiddish-derived American slang for a pest or a tediously dull person.

clue.text: Person who is promising to protect cypher is a nut

indicators.note: to protect something is to surround and shield it

parts.note: a comer is someone showing promise
a cypher is a code

explanation.surface: Someone who vows to guard a secret code is clearly crazy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a nut' looks like a crank; it is a real nut.
explanation.definitionFit: The coco-de-mer is the huge double coconut of the Seychelles palm.

clue.text: Chooses old points

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for old
pts is the abbreviation for points

explanation.surface: Someone picks out some well-worn arguments.
explanation.definitionFit: To opt is to choose or decide in favour of one option.

clue.text: Nothing in new-fangled pattern? I would assess that

indicators.note: in means one thing is placed inside the other
new-fangled suggests something remade in a novel form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Is there nothing in this fancy new design? Someone offers to judge.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition answers the question: whether a new design has anything novel in it is what one granting patents assesses.
explanation.definitionFit: A patentor grants patents, so they judge whether an invention is genuinely new.

clue.text: Chance missed by inside left on the wing

indicators.note: inside means the small word sits within the other one
on the wing means in flight, letters in motion that settle in a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
a work by someone is a work of theirs

explanation.surface: A football inside left, playing out wide, misses an opening.
explanation.walkthrough: Inside left and wing are football positions, which hides the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A let-off is a failure to take advantage, like a dropped catch that spares the batsman.

clue.text: Frank carries a lot for a cool walk

indicators.note: carries means the first word holds the other inside it

parts.note: frank means free, open
scads are lots, a large amount

explanation.surface: A man named Frank hauls a heavy load on a fresh stroll.
explanation.definitionFit: A frescade is a shady, cool walk, from the Italian for fresh air.

clue.text: Jumping Jack, an Irish Catholic

parts.note: jack and salt are both slang for a sailor
the indefinite article
a tory was originally an Irish Catholic outlaw of the 17th century

explanation.surface: Jumping Jack, an Irish Catholic, sounds like a nickname for a lively person.
explanation.walkthrough: The word Tory began as a name for dispossessed Irish Catholic outlaws.
explanation.definitionFit: Saltatory means relating to leaping or dancing, proceeding by jumps.

clue.text: Number missing exploding golden rain firework

indicators.note: exploding blows the letters apart so they land in a new order
missing means the abbreviation is left out of the letters

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for number
taken as written

explanation.surface: A golden-rain firework is missing from the set going off.
explanation.walkthrough: Golden rain is itself a kind of firework, which makes it look like the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A girandole is a rotating firework wheel throwing out jets of fire.

clue.text: Rising hostel singers not entirely in minor keys

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means read from the bottom upwards
the answer lies only partly within each of the two words

parts.note: letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: Youth hostel singers climb into songs in minor keys.
explanation.walkthrough: 'minor keys' sounds musical; a key is a low island, also spelt cay.
explanation.definitionFit: Islets are small islands, and keys or cays are small low islands too.

clue.text: African one's seen in two neighbouring US states close to Canada

indicators.note: seen in means placed between, inside the pair

parts.note: the postal codes of New York and New Jersey, which border each other
a means one

indicators.note: the close of a word is its final letter

parts.note: last letter

explanation.surface: An African person turns up in two adjoining states near the Canadian border.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nyanja are a Bantu-speaking people of Malawi and Zambia, so an African.

clue.text: Muslim students in strain without lecturer

indicators.note: in means one group sits inside the other word

parts.note: seil is Scots for to strain; lecturer L goes

indicators.note: without means the abbreviation is removed

parts.note: the National Union of Students
L is an abbreviation for lecturer

explanation.surface: Muslim students are under strain with no lecturer to teach them.
explanation.definitionFit: A Senusi is a member of a North African Muslim brotherhood founded in the 19th century.

clue.text: Nothing's accepted in supplements, causing dispute

indicators.note: accepted in tells the solver to admit a letter into the word in place of an existing one

parts.note: adds means supplements, as a verb
O for nothing, replacing the leading A

explanation.surface: Accepting nothing in the way of extras leads to a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: The A of the verb for supplements is swapped for O; no word in the clue marks which letter goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Odds can mean a dispute or disagreement, as in being at odds.

clue.text: Rodent picked up a toadstool top

indicators.note: in a down clue, picked up means lifted so the letters read upwards

parts.note: taken as written
the cap is the top of a mushroom or toadstool

explanation.surface: A rodent snatches up the top of a toadstool.
explanation.definitionFit: The paca is a large South American rodent related to the agouti.

clue.text: Charm previously Poles missed in bustling Bosnia

indicators.note: bustling suggests busy movement, stirring the letters into a new order
missed means these letters are left out of the word

parts.note: S and N, the south and north poles
taken as written

explanation.surface: Charming Polish visitors were missed in busy Bosnia some time ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'previously' belongs to the definition: obia is an old variant spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Obia is an earlier form of obeah, a fetish or charm in West Indian folk magic.

clue.text: Old dukes finished with party, Times put out

indicators.note: put out means those letters are thrown out of the words

parts.note: neat means finished, polished; the T goes
a fest is a party; the T goes
T is the abbreviation for time, so two Ts

explanation.surface: Elderly dukes, done with the party, are thrown out by the newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: Dukes is slang for fists, so 'Old dukes' asks for an archaic word for fists.
explanation.definitionFit: Neafe is an obsolete word for fist, and dukes is slang for the fists.

clue.text: Black and slack by the sound of it

indicators.note: by the sound of it means the word is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: slack means slow, sluggish

explanation.surface: Black and lazy, so it seems.
explanation.definitionFit: The sloe is the black fruit of the blackthorn, and sloe means a deep blue-black colour.

clue.text: High official abroad accepted bill, for example

parts.note: A is an abbreviation for accepted
a tab is a bill, as at a bar
e.g. is the abbreviation for for example

explanation.surface: A senior official overseas has signed off his expenses bill, for one.
explanation.definitionFit: An atabeg was a Turkish or Persian governor or high-ranking prince's guardian.

clue.text: Drive miles into remote parts of Asia for this tree?

indicators.note: to drive one thing into another is to force it inside
the remote parts of a word are its two far ends

parts.note: first and last letters
ml is a Chambers abbreviation for miles

explanation.surface: Should one drive miles into the far reaches of Asia to find this tree?
explanation.definitionFit: The amla is the Indian gooseberry, a tree of South Asia bearing sour fruit.

clue.text: A lot of civility shown by adjutant and one Balkan guerilla

indicators.note: a lot of means most but not all, so the last letter is cut

parts.note: comity is civility, courteous relations; its last letter goes
adj. is the abbreviation for adjutant
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An army adjutant and a Balkan partisan show each other great courtesy.
explanation.definitionFit: A comitadji was a member of an irregular guerrilla band in the Balkans.

clue.text: Buffalo's belly uncovered

indicators.note: uncovered means stripped of its outer letters at each end

parts.note: Chambers gives carnal as relating to the belly; both ends go

explanation.surface: A buffalo's underside is exposed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buffalo's belly' reads as one phrase; the 's is just is.
explanation.definitionFit: The arna is the wild water buffalo of India.

clue.text: Always stick around for Indian millet

indicators.note: around means turned about, so the letters read backwards

parts.note: e'er is poetic for ever, always
to stick is to stab or jab

explanation.surface: A cook always gives Indian millet a stir.
explanation.definitionFit: Bajree, also bajra, is pearl millet, a cereal grown in India.
